newsitem.title: INDIA: India could buy power from Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: India could buy power from Pakistan.

text.p: Power-starved India plans to buy a large amount of electricity from neighbouring Pakistan as part of increased cooperation between the longtime arch-rivals, officials said.
Junior Power Minister S. Venugopalachari said India could begin buying 3,000 megawatts of surplus power from its neighbour as early as next year.
"We are planning to buy 3,000 megawatts by 1998-99," Venugopalachari told reporters in the southern city of Bangalore late on Sunday.
Last week Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, held talks on the margins of a regional summit in the Maldives.

Gujral later cited the purchase of surplus energy from Pakistan as one of the agreements that could be reached in talks between the longtime foes, which have fought three wars since 1947. He did not say how much power could be bought.
The foreign secretaries -- the nations' highest ranking career diplomats -- are expected to hold talks in late June in Islamabad.
Venugopalachari said the Power Ministry would work out the tariff structure for buying Pakistani electricity, generated by three hydroelectric plants in the Indus River basin to the west of India.

"Right now, discussions are on between the external affairs ministries. Next month a team of our officials will be visiting Pakistan, after which further discussion at ministerial levels will take place," Venugopalachari said.
Venugopalachari said rivers in northeastern India had the potential to generate about 30,000 megawatts of power, part of which India was considering selling to Bangladesh.
He said the Asia Development Bank had already started a feasibility study for building transmission lines between eastern Indian states and Bangladesh.
